name: manual_9cc7ae
claim: When a code review lists multiple findings, checking each one against the actual current file content before fixing it is not a formality -- in a real remediation pass, roughly half of a review's findings can already be correctly handled in current code (fixed by an earlier commit, or never actually present as described), and treating every finding as needing action wastes effort and risks introducing unnecessary or even incorrect changes to code that was already right. The check itself is cheap (grep or read the exact lines cited); skipping it in favor of blindly applying every suggested diff is the expensive mistake.

decisions.notes: Verify-before-fix discipline paid off concretely this remediation pass -- roughly half the findings didn't need action.

rationale: Verify-before-fix discipline paid off concretely this remediation pass -- roughly half the findings didn't need action.
